question.text: Chapter 9 describes MBO (Management Buyout) as a common form of LBO. In the example given, ABC is a listed entity where management holds 25% and the public holds 75%. For a valid MBO per the workbook example, management must end up holding:

answer.text: At least 51% (controlling interest) — by purchasing enough shares from the public.
At least 10% to keep operational skin-in-the-game.
Exactly 100% — all public shareholders must be squeezed out.
At least 75% — equivalent to a takeover delisting threshold.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook example states that the current management will purchase enough shares from the public so that it can end up holding at least 51% of the stock. The defining feature of an MBO in the workbook is reaching the 51% control threshold, not a full buyout. The Trap: 10% is well below control. 100% goes beyond the workbook example. 75% borrows from delisting-threshold context that is not the basis for the MBO example. Note: The MBO example appears on page 210; the workbook does not prescribe a post-close management equity-plan size or ESOP/phantom-unit percentage.
